Live-edge slab about 1.8 to 2 m long, about 25 to 35 cm wide, very pale, with a ragged broken (not sawn) chunk out of one side near the middle, several splits near the top, and scattered small dark pinholes and specks over the face. Pinholes can mean borer or ambrosia beetle, which is a mild flag because Huon pine's oil usually resists insects, though fine specks can also be grit. Species unproven.
